clue.text: Team ten divers? You need some publicity for that!

indicators.note: the question 'Team ten divers?' asks what those words could become; 'for that' points the solver back at them as letters to rework

explanation.surface: A team of ten divers would need to advertise to fill its places.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no conventional anagram word: the question mark after 'Team ten divers' and 'for that' tell you to rearrange all thirteen letters of those three words.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert in a paper or on air is one piece of promotion, a portion of publicity.

clue.text: Doubtful call over debts

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, on top of, the second

parts.note: to dub someone is to give them a name, to call them something
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: A ruling on what is owed is questionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubtful and dubious are synonyms, both meaning open to question or uncertain.

clue.text: Direction which every thoroughfare takes

parts.note: EA is the standard abbreviation for each, which here stands for every
ST is short for street, a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: Asking which way every road happens to run.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four compass points, a direction of travel.

clue.text: Fabrics one may want when suffering from cold

definitions.text: one may want when suffering from cold

explanation.surface: Cloth that comes in handy when you have a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine, delicate woven cloths are tissues; soft paper handkerchiefs used for a runny nose are also tissues.

clue.text: Wild men or wise men in Virginia

indicators.note: the Virginia abbreviation sits inside the word for wise men

parts.note: sages are wise men
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Contrasting untamed folk with learned ones living in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Savages is an old, now offensive, term for supposedly uncivilised or untamed people.

clue.text: It's salad dressing in America and in Ireland

explanation.surface: A word that names a condiment in the States and a place in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans shorten mayonnaise to mayo; Mayo is also a county in the west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Flower offered to domestic goddess

explanation.surface: A bloom presented to a woman who excels at home-making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic goddess' is Nigella Lawson, the British TV cook famous for that phrase from her book title.
explanation.definitionFit: Love-in-a-mist is a blue garden bloom of this genus; the cook Nigella Lawson is nicknamed for her book How to Be a Domestic Goddess.

clue.text: Circulating slander among corps leads to gossip

indicators.note: circulating means moving round, so the letters are stirred into a new order
the leads of a word are its opening letters, here just the first one of corps

explanation.surface: Defamatory talk going round a military unit leads to rumour-mongering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulating' shuffles SLANDER and AMONG together with C, the first letter of 'corps' picked out by 'leads'; 'to' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who spreads malicious rumours is a gossip, a teller of tales.

clue.text: Relax in the fresh air?

parts.note: read literally it is about drawing in lungfuls of outdoor air without strain; the phrase also means to stop worrying

explanation.surface: Unwinding outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to feel relieved after anxiety, and literally to take in air without effort.

clue.text: Painters of a little lion, first and second

parts.note: a young lion is a cub
1ST is first; the figure 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Artists depicting a lion cub, ranked in order.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure in 1ST is written as the letter I, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso and Braque founded Cubism, so its practitioners are painters of that school.

clue.text: Traveller on a cruise to Russia

parts.note: a sea cruise is a voyage
R is the abbreviation for Russia

explanation.surface: Someone taking a sea trip bound for Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone making a long journey, especially by sea, is a traveller.

clue.text: A corner to play in Japan, all right?

parts.note: Noh (also spelt No) is the classical masked drama of Japan
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Asking whether a quiet spot to put on a show in Japan is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A small recess or secluded spot is a corner, a little alcove.

clue.text: Swell material, we hear!

indicators.note: says the word for the cloth is only spoken, and the answer is its sound-alike

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled cloth

explanation.surface: An exclamation that some cloth is wonderful, by report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' reads as the slang adjective for excellent, but it is the noun or verb for a rise in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden rush or rise, as a swell is a rolling upward movement of water.

clue.text: Able to turn back from island

indicators.note: the word Able is to be read in the opposite direction, last letter first

explanation.surface: Being capable of retreating from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Napoleon was exiled to this Mediterranean island off Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is the Italian island in the Tyrrhenian Sea where Napoleon was first exiled.

clue.text: London police get about more than the yard

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Police, London's force
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Officers in the capital roam beyond Scotland Yard's walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The yard' suggests Scotland Yard, the police headquarters; it is the unit of length, about 91 cm.
explanation.definitionFit: This metric unit of about 39.4 inches is slightly longer than 36 inches.

clue.text: Disconcert by having a party

parts.note: a bash is a lively party

explanation.surface: Throwing people off balance by holding a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To embarrass or discomfit someone is to disconcert them.

clue.text: Simple responses needed here

parts.note: points at the grid itself: this puzzle is the Simple, not the Cryptic, and needs replies written into its lights

explanation.surface: A form asking only for basic replies.
explanation.definitionFit: Replies to questions are what solvers enter, and every grid needs them filled in.

clue.text: In Sweden, pop group gets time (an hour) on Sunday

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
ABBA is the famous Swedish pop group
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: In Sweden, the band gets an hour's slot on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places ABBA in Sweden, but 'In Sweden' simply gives its own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: For most Christians the day of rest and worship is Sunday.

clue.text: Chant softly while setting snare

parts.note: a mantra is a sacred phrase that is chanted
p (piano) is the musical marking for softly

explanation.surface: Murmuring a chant while laying a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap set to catch intruders or poachers is a snare.

clue.text: A new look for Ivor

parts.note: novel means new
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Fresh styling for a man called Ivor.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor; the Ivor Novello Awards for songwriting are named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname completes the stage name of the entertainer Ivor Novello.

clue.text: Bachelor's home — a lodge in Cornwall

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat, typically a single man's
to stow is to lodge or store something

explanation.surface: A single man's flat, a cottage down in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the south-western tip of England; Padstow is a fishing port there.
explanation.definitionFit: Padstow is a harbour town on the north coast of the county of Cornwall, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Cut some clothes out!

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: An order to remove some garments.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit worn for a period, role or nation is a set of clothes.

clue.text: A capital officer — boom out the name!

parts.note: Col is short for colonel, an army officer

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of boom are disordered

explanation.surface: An officer in a big city bellows out a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The name' adds to the surface only: the city was the capital of Sri Lanka.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombo is the chief city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Suffer in the channel tunnel?

explanation.surface: Enduring hardship beneath the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as UNDER GO: travellers in the Channel Tunnel go beneath the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure or experience something unpleasant is to suffer it; read as two words it describes travelling below the water.

clue.text: Part of the church is in western avenue

indicators.note: says the answer sits inside the words western avenue, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A church's main space lies on a road in the west.
explanation.definitionFit: The central body of a church, where the congregation sits, is one section of the building.

clue.text: Loved ones taking marriage vow outside Leeds

indicators.note: the vow stands outside, ahead of, the Leeds letters

parts.note: I do is the vow spoken at a wedding
LS is the postcode area for Leeds

explanation.surface: Sweethearts exchanging wedding vows on the edge of Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, northern England, whose postcodes begin LS.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are adored or worshipped, heroes and favourites, are loved ones.

clue.text: Identification at two points on certain dates

parts.note: E and S are two compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: Showing papers at two places on particular days.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ides were the 15th of March, May, July and October and the 13th of other months in the Roman calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the ides fell on fixed days of each month, so particular calendar days.

clue.text: The two take nothing from the stall

indicators.note: take, with from, says the letter for nothing is subtracted

parts.note: a booth is a market stall
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A pair helps themselves to nothing from a market stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both means each of a pair, the two together.

clue.text: Man maybe needing a bit of land

explanation.surface: A man in want of a small plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland; 'maybe' flags it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is one example; any island is a small piece of ground surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Another fish will make a face at the burbot

parts.note: an eel is a fish, other than the one defined
to pout is to push out the lips, making a face

explanation.surface: One fish grimaces at another.
explanation.definitionFit: Eelpout is an alternative common name for the burbot, a freshwater cod.

clue.text: Wind then fog — painter left finally

indicators.note: finally puts the letter for left at the end

parts.note: mist is a light fog
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: A weather report: gale, then fog, and an artist departed in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a cold northerly wind blowing down the Rhône valley into southern France.

clue.text: Make a pig of oneself — and do it thoroughly!

explanation.surface: Gorging, and doing so with total commitment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to commit fully; taken literally it suggests eating an entire pig, greedily overeating.
